newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 tumbles as major issues lose support.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 tumbles as major issues lose support.

text.p: Czech shares tumbled on Tuesday with dealers struggling to find an explanation other than a knock-on effect from sharp overnight losses on Wall Street.

"I didn't find out anything fundamentally new or wrong about any of the companies except...rumours about Temelin and CEZ. But with Komercni and Telecom I don't see anything new, just poor bid on the market," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.

CEZ has been hit in recent days by rumours that its Temelin nuclear power plant may cost an extra eight billion crowns to complete. But after heavy losses earlier in the day it closed up one crown at 901.

Kusacek said Wall Street may have been to blame for the performance of other major issues, all of which closed lower, but added that continued worries about the Czech crown were also holding foreign investors back.
"It's something to do with Wall Street but foreign investors still think the crown may go slightly lower and maybe expectation of this is creating room for the falls," he said.
The crown has held steady since the central bank (CNB) floated it at the end of May but its policy of gradually cutting interest rates has caused concern about the currency's fate in the longer term.
